deferredRelationshipFields.status: null in every canonical entity (Phase 3A) — deferred as a cross-entity computation, out of scope for a per-entity builder. The adapter has nothing to expose because the source has nothing; this is reported explicitly, not synthesized to look populated.

provenancePreservation.approach: The legacy flat-record shape itself never had a provenance concept (data/names.json and data/names-enriched.json rows carry no field indicating researched-vs-computed) — the adapter does not invent one, since that would not be reproducing legacy behavior, it would be adding new behavior under a legacy name.
provenancePreservation.whereProvenanceActuallyLives: Fully preserved and recoverable from the canonical source: every leaf field's x-provenance annotation lives in schemas/name-entity.schema.json (Phase 2A), and audit/canonical-build-report.json (Phase 3A) already reports provenanceFieldCounts (21 computed, 29 researched) read directly from that schema. The adapter sits downstream of that and does not need to re-expose it in the legacy shape to preserve it upstream.
provenancePreservation.verified: A caller needing provenance for a field the adapter exposes can consult data/canonical/names.json directly (the adapter's own input) rather than the adapted legacy-shape output — this was a deliberate design choice, not an oversight, and is documented in docs/ADAPTER_LAYER.md.

coverageSummary.note: 8 of 18 canonical domains have at least one field reaching the legacy shape; this ratio is expected and correct, not a coverage failure — the legacy shape itself only ever had ~13 flat fields plus 3 relational datasets, so it structurally cannot represent domains (etymology, history, culture, religion, nicknames, citations, relatedNames, relationships) that never existed in the legacy model.
